# Service Engineer Academy

> Online, self-paced courses for medical equipment service engineers (biomedical / HTM / field service): MRI, CT, X-ray, ultrasound, anesthesia, ventilators, dialysis, defibrillators, lab, dental and more. Each course has short lessons with figures, a timed final exam and a verifiable certificate. Operated by Service Engineer Ltd (Astana International Financial Centre, Kazakhstan). Prices in USD, pay by card (Paddle) or by company invoice. Contact: ceo@serviceengineer.app

Who it is for: in-house biomedical / clinical engineering staff, independent service organizations (ISOs), field service engineers, technical experts who investigate equipment failures, and managers who need documented training of their engineers.

Team access: every course can be bought for a team; companies can request an offer and invoice at https://serviceengineer.academy/quote/

## Courses

- [Aeonmed Aeon 7200 / 7200A Anaesthesia Machine — Model Service](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/aeon-7200/) — Model; 5 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. A model course for engineers who have passed Anaesthesia Workstation Service — Level 1. It takes the Aeon 7200A apart on paper: pipeline and cylinder inputs, the pneumatic O2 failure warning and N2O cut-off, the flowmeter bank with its O2-N2O link, the vaporiser manifold, the circle and absorber, the bellows and the O2-driven ventilator with its sensors, boards and battery. Then the engineer's checkout with your own instruments against the manufacturer's values, the maintenance schedule and its gaps, fault-finding from alarm group and test point to a proven part, and a complete return to service with electrical safety and a record. Independent course: not affiliated with or endorsed by Beijing Aeonmed Co., Ltd. Aeonmed and Aeon are trademarks of their owner; other names are trademarks of their respective owners.
- [Anaesthesia Machine Service — Level 2: Fault-Finding](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/anes-l2/) — Level 2; 8 lessons, 5 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Level 1 taught you to check, maintain and verify an anaesthesia workstation. Level 2 starts when the checkout fails anyway, or passes while the anaesthetist still complains. This course teaches the engineer to read the checkout result and the machine's log as evidence, split the machine into gas supply, flow control, vaporisers, breathing system, ventilator and monitoring, and separate them with a test lung, an analyser and the machine's own tests until one module is left - and then prove the repair and write down who decides that the machine is fit for use.
- [Angiography and C-arm Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/angio-l1/) — Level 1; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. Mobile C-arms wear out from transport and handling long before their tube does, and fixed angiography rooms stop on a potentiometer, a brake or a lost connection far more often than on a failed generator. This course teaches the engineer who maintains C-arms and angiography systems to keep them safe for staff and patients, to understand the imaging chain well enough to tell a fault from a setting, and to run a planned maintenance that finds wear before the surgeon does.
- [Angiography and C-arm Service — Level 2: Fault-Finding](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/angio-l2/) — Level 2; 8 lessons, 5 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Level 1 taught you to keep a C-arm or an angiography room safe, maintained and measured. Level 2 starts when it fails anyway, usually with a patient on the table. This course teaches the engineer to read the logs of mobile C-arms and fixed angiography systems for the first and causal event, to isolate the fault between the stand and the workstation, the generator and the tube, the image chain and the detector, the motion system and the software, and to follow it to the module that has really failed. Then it shows how to return the system to clinical use with the tests, dose checks, safety tests and written records that prove the repair.
- [bioMérieux mini VIDAS Immunoassay Analyser — Model Service](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/biomerieux-mini-vidas/) — Model; 5 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. A model course for engineers who have passed Lab Analyser Service — Level 1, and ideally Level 2. It takes the mini VIDAS apart on paper: the ELFA strip and SPR, the two independent sections with their heated blocks, trays and six-channel pipettors, the flash-lamp fluorometer on its moving scanner, the solid standard and auto-calibration, and the three levels of controller boards. Then the work itself: start-up, temperature and QCT checks, calibration strips and what QC proves, the annual maintenance in the right order, fault-finding from the four error groups to one section and one assembly, part replacement with the follow-up each part needs, the section, scanner and optics adjustments, and a return to service that waits for the laboratory's standards and QC. Independent course: not affiliated with or endorsed by bioMérieux. bioMérieux, VIDAS and mini VIDAS are trademarks of their owner; other names are trademarks of their respective owners.

Its gantry, couch and consoles by the names its documentation uses, the warm-up and calibration order, the backups that save a reinstall, the PM wear points engineers actually find, fault-finding from over kV to a degraded RAID, and tube, disk and software replacement with the calibrations and checks before release. Built on resolved field cases. Independent course: not affiliated with or endorsed by Canon Medical Systems or Toshiba. Canon, Toshiba and Aquilion are trademarks of their owners.

- [CT Service — Level 2: Fault-Finding](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/ct-l2/) — Level 2; 10 lessons, 6 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Level 1 taught you to keep a CT scanner safe, calibrated and maintained. Level 2 starts when it stops anyway. This course teaches the engineer to read the error log for the first error rather than the loudest, place the failure in the scan sequence, and follow it through the tube, the high-voltage generator, the slip ring, the detector, the gantry, the table and the computers to the subsystem that has actually failed - and then prove the repair with the calibrations, phantom tests and records the manufacturer requires.
- [Defibrillator and ECG Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/defib-l1/) — Level 1; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. Most defibrillators that fail on the ward fail for small reasons: a tired battery, expired pads, a cracked cable, a sync button left on, a self-test warning nobody read. This course teaches the engineer who looks after manual defibrillators, AEDs and ECG machines to work safely around stored high energy, to test delivered energy, charge time and synchronised cardioversion with an analyser, to keep devices ready between uses, and to find the common ECG and printer faults.
- [Defibrillator and ECG Service — Level 2: Fault-Finding](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/defib-l2/) — Level 2; 8 lessons, 5 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Level 1 taught you to test a defibrillator with an analyser, keep its battery and pads in date and find the common ECG faults. Level 2 starts when the device fails anyway. This course teaches the engineer to read self-test and event logs for the first cause, to separate power, charge, storage, delivery and monitoring with the cheapest test that tells them apart, to follow the fault to the battery, the charger, the capacitor, the switching stage, the cable, the pacer, the ECG front end or the printer, and to return the device to service with the measurements and records that prove it. Stored energy is treated as the first hazard in every lesson.
- [Dental Equipment Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/dental-l1/) — Level 1; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. A wet compressor, a clogged filter in the floor box, a suction unit full of foam, a handpiece oiled the wrong way - most dental calls start with something outside the part that gets blamed. This course teaches the engineer who maintains a dental practice to see the whole installation and keep it safe and working.
- [Dental Equipment Service — Level 2: Fault-Finding](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/dental-l2/) — Level 2; 8 lessons, 5 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Level 1 taught you to see the whole dental installation and keep it safe and maintained. Level 2 starts when something stops anyway. This course teaches the engineer to read the code and the symptom, place the fault on a map of air, water, suction, power and control, prove it with a gauge, a meter or a swap, and follow it through the unit, the handpieces, the compressor and suction plant, the intraoral, panoramic and CBCT X-ray units and the autoclave to the part that has actually failed - and then return the equipment to service with the tests and records that show it is fit for patients.
- [Dialysis Equipment Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/dialysis-l1/) — Level 1; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. A dialysis machine is the last link in a chain that starts at the city water inlet. Poor water, a wrong concentrate, a reused filter or a conductivity system that agrees with itself and is wrong can all harm a patient while every screen looks normal. This course teaches the engineer who maintains dialysis equipment to keep the whole chain safe, verified and documented.
- [Dialysis Equipment Service — Level 2: Fault-Finding](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/dialysis-l2/) — Level 2; 8 lessons, 5 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Level 1 taught you to keep a dialysis unit safe, disinfected and maintained. Level 2 starts when a machine keeps failing anyway. This course teaches the engineer to read the alarm and self-test history for the first cause, trace the fault on the hydraulic diagram of the exact machine, split the blood side from the dialysate side and the machine from its water and concentrate supply, and follow the fault through pumps, valves, degassing, balancing, conductivity, the heater, the blood module, disinfection and the water plant to the part that has really failed, without ever weakening a protective system. It ends with peritoneal cyclers, multi-cause cases and the tests and records that let the responsible person decide whether a machine may treat patients again.
- [Digital X-ray Detectors — Level 2](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/dr-detectors/) — Level 2; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. A calibration taken with the grid in place, a wireless link that gives up half a second too early, a battery that is not the original, a panel that was stood on — most 'dead detector' calls start with something that can be found in an hour if you know where to look. This course teaches the engineer who already services X-ray rooms to understand flat-panel detectors from the inside, keep them calibrated, read their artefacts, integrate them with generators and networks, and tell a real detector failure from everything that only looks like one.

- [Endoscopy Equipment Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/endo-l1/) — Level 1; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. A bitten insertion tube, a skipped leak test, a scope soaked with the wrong cap, a lamp run past its life, a washer whose hose has been dissolving for a year — most endoscopy downtime and most expensive repairs start with handling, reprocessing and simple checks that nobody owned. This course teaches the engineer who looks after an endoscopy unit how the tower, the scopes and the reprocessing equipment work, what to check, and what to hand on to a specialist.
- [Endoscopy Equipment Service — Level 2: Fault-Finding](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/endo-l2/) — Level 2; 8 lessons, 5 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Level 1 taught you how the tower, the scopes and the reprocessors work and how to check them. Level 2 starts when the check fails and the obvious swap does not help. This course teaches the engineer to read the processor and reprocessor logs, run swap tests that actually separate two suspects, follow the image and light chains to the failed board, lamp, cable or seal, localise a leak or an angulation fault in a flexible scope, decide honestly what can be repaired in the field and what must go to a specialist, and return the equipment to service with tests and records that hold up.

- [Electrosurgery Service — Level 2: Fault-Finding](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/esu-l2/) — Level 2; 8 lessons, 4 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. After a burn or a fire, it teaches you to preserve the evidence first.
- [Fault-Finding Method for Medical Equipment](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/fault-finding-method/) — General; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $49 per engineer, team of 5 $190. A sterilizer that aborts with a vacuum error and turns out to have a flat backup battery. A CT detector that reboots at random while seven good boards are replaced. A test that fails because the wrong test bag was used. Most lost hours in service are not lost on hard faults; they are lost on guessing. This course teaches the loop that experienced engineers run in their heads on every job: collect the facts, list the hypotheses, choose the cheapest test that separates them, measure instead of assuming, find the root cause, and return the machine to service safely with a report that the next engineer can use. Every lesson is built on real resolved cases from MRI, CT, X-ray, ultrasound, laboratory, sterilization, dental, anaesthesia and ventilation equipment.

- [Power and Cooling for Medical Equipment](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/infra-l1/) — Repair fundamentals; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. CT, MRI, angiography and X-ray systems depend on things their manufacturer does not build: the mains supply and earthing, the UPS and generator, the chiller and its water loops, and the air conditioning of the scan room and equipment room. When one of them weakens, the scanner shows it as a tube that will not cool, a gradient that trips, a magnet that loses helium or a console that freezes. This course teaches the engineer to see the site behind the machine, to find infrastructure faults by method, to work safely on UPS battery banks and mains equipment, and to keep power and cooling under planned maintenance together with the facility team and the manufacturer.
- [Power and Cooling for Medical Equipment — Level 2: Fault-Finding](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/infra-l2/) — Level 2; 8 lessons, 5 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Level 1 taught you to see the building behind the scanner: the supply, the UPS, the chiller, the loops and the room air, and who owns each of them. Level 2 starts when one of those links has failed and everybody says it is somebody else's. This course teaches the engineer to put the logs of the scanner, the UPS and the chiller on one timeline, to prove which link failed with recordings and trends, and then to follow the fault inside that link: rectifier, inverter, bypass and battery string in the UPS; sags, neutral and earth faults, generators and transfer switches in the supply; compressor, condenser, expansion and pressure faults in the chiller; pumps, flow switches, strainers, air and water quality in the loops; and the HVAC of the scan and equipment rooms. It ends where the real work ends: restarting an imaging system safely after a power or cooling failure, with the checks and records that prove it is ready.
- [Infusion and Syringe Pump Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/infusion-l1/) — Level 1; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. Infusion and syringe pumps are the most numerous powered devices in a hospital, and they deliver drugs where a few millilitres too many or too few matter. Most faults are mundane: a syringe the pump does not like, a tired battery, a sticky key, dried glucose in the mechanism. This course teaches the engineer to tell a real pump fault from a set or use problem, to test flow, occlusion and air detection properly, and to hand a pump back only when it is safe.

It takes the R Series ALS, Plus and BLS apart on paper: the system brick with its digital and analog boards and the PD engine with its capacitor, the OneStep cable and electrode family, the SurePower battery and charger, the printer and the monitoring options; what the Code Readiness system tests and what it leaves to you; the annual checkout with an analyser and what each result means on this waveform; battery and accessory maintenance; fault-finding from the message on the screen to an accessory, a setting or a replaceable assembly; and a safe repair and return to service with data, software and configuration handled correctly. Independent course: not affiliated with or endorsed by ZOLL Medical Corporation. ZOLL, R Series, OneStep, SurePower, Code-Ready and CodeNet are trademarks of their owner; other names are trademarks of their respective owners.
- [ZOLL X Series Monitor/Defibrillator — Model Service](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/zoll-x-series/) — Model; 5 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. A model course for engineers who have passed Defibrillator and ECG Service — Level 1. It takes the X Series and X Series Advanced apart on paper: the monitor board with its three processors and power system, the two-board defibrillator module and the capacitor, the NIBP, EtCO2, SpO2, IBP and temperature options, the printer, the communications carrier and the SurePower battery; what the Ready For Use indicator and the readiness test prove and what they leave to you; the 25-step annual test sequence with an analyser and simulators and the acceptance values that go with it; battery, cable and accessory upkeep; fault-finding from the message on the screen to an accessory, a setting or one module; and a safe repair and return to service, with restricted parts, data, software and electrical safety handled correctly. Independent course: not affiliated with or endorsed by ZOLL Medical Corporation. ZOLL, X Series, SurePower and Rectilinear Biphasic are trademarks of their owner; Masimo, Rainbow, Oridion and Microstream are trademarks of their respective owners.
- [Medicine for Engineers](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/med-eng/) — General; 8 lessons, 4 h, certificate; $49 per engineer, team of 5 $190. Every device you repair measures or supports something in a human body. If you do not know what that something is, you cannot tell a fault from a patient, a misleading reading from a real one, or an urgent call from a loud one. This course gives the service engineer the medicine behind the equipment: how a hospital works, what images show, what the heart, lungs and blood tell the clinician, why anaesthesia and intensive care leave no time for failure, how not to carry infection, and how to turn a clinician's complaint into a technical question you can test.
- [Physics of Medical Equipment](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/physics/) — General; 10 lessons, 5 h, certificate; $49 per engineer, team of 5 $190. A noisy MRI image, a chiller alarm, a dead line on an ultrasound picture, a leak test that fails by a few millilitres: each of these is physics before it is a part number. This course takes the physics a service engineer actually uses — electricity and fields, waves and radiation, sound, magnetic resonance, cryogenics, gases, light, heat and measurement — and explains each through the machine it lives in and the symptom it produces when something goes wrong.
- [Electrical Safety for Medical Equipment](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/esafety/) — General; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $79 per engineer, team of 5 $290. Every repaired device goes back to a patient. Electrical safety testing is the last line between your repair and that patient — and it is also the test most often done as a formality. This course explains why the limits exist, how the analyzer measures, and how to test and document properly after repair and at every PM.
- [Pneumatics and Medical Gases — Repair Fundamentals](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/pneumatics/) — Repair fundamentals; 8 lessons, 5 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. Ventilators, anaesthesia workstations, suction units, concentrators, dental chairs and laboratory analysers are built from the same pneumatic parts: regulators, valves, sensors, seals and the gas supply that feeds them. This course teaches the trade they share - how each part works, how it fails, how to test it on the bench, how to find a leak by method rather than luck, and how to repair and prove the repair without creating an oxygen hazard.
- [Electronics and Power Supplies — Repair Fundamentals](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/electronics/) — Repair fundamentals; 10 lessons, 6 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. Monitors, ultrasound systems, infusion pumps, ventilators and X-ray generators share the same electronics: switch-mode supplies, regulators, batteries, processor boards, buses, cables and connectors. This course teaches the trade they have in common — working safely on the bench, reading schematics, using instruments correctly, and finding the failed board and the failed component by method rather than by swapping parts until the fault goes away.
- [MRI Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/mri-l1/) — Level 1; 8 lessons, 4 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. A healthy MRI magnet loses almost no helium: the cold head turns the boil-off back into liquid. When the cold head, the compressor or the chiller stops, the level starts to fall — and nobody notices until it is expensive. This course teaches the engineer who services the scanner to see it coming.
- [CT Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/ct-l1/) — Level 1; 8 lessons, 4 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Air conditioning, dirty filters, a skipped air calibration, a slip ring nobody cleaned — most CT failures start with something cheap that nobody checked. This course teaches the engineer who maintains a CT scanner to keep it safe, calibrated and running.
- [Ultrasound Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/us-l1/) — Level 1; 8 lessons, 4 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Probes are dropped, bent, soaked in the wrong disinfectant and plugged in hot. This course teaches the engineer to test probes, judge image quality, maintain the system and tell a probe fault from a system fault in minutes.
- [Ultrasound Service — Level 2: Fault-Finding](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/us-l2/) — Level 2; 10 lessons, 6 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Level 1 taught you to test a probe. Level 2 starts when the probe is innocent. This course teaches the engineer to move a fault before touching a screwdriver, read the logs and built-in tests, and follow the symptom through the front end, the beamformer, the power chain and the PC to the one module that has failed - then prove the repair with a phantom and a safety test.
- [Ultrasound Probes — Testing, Diagnosis and Repair Decisions](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/us-probes/) — Probe repair; 8 lessons, 5 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. Probes are dropped, crushed, soaked and bitten, and they cost as much as a car. This course takes the engineer inside the probe: how it is built, how each layer fails, how to test it with and without a probe tester, how to clear endocavity and TEE probes electrically, how mechanical 4D and TEE probes fail, and how to decide - on evidence - between repair, replacement and withdrawal.
- [Ventilator Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/vent-l1/) — Level 1; 8 lessons, 4 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. The self-test checks the machine against itself. Only an independent gas-flow analyzer on a test lung tells you what the patient would actually receive. This course teaches the engineer who maintains ICU ventilators to keep them safe: gas supply, pneumatics, the PM kit, and the verification that must follow every repair.
- [Anaesthesia Workstation Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/anes-l1/) — Level 1; 8 lessons, 4 h, certificate; $149 per engineer, team of 5 $590. An anaesthesia workstation is a gas system, a ventilator, a monitor and a set of safety interlocks in one cart. This course teaches the engineer to follow the gas path, run leak and checkout tests properly, maintain the machine and verify it before it goes back to theatre.
- [Patient Monitor Service — Level 1](https://serviceengineer.academy/course/mon-l1/) — Level 1; 6 lessons, 3 h, certificate; $99 per engineer, team of 5 $390. ECG, SpO2, NIBP, IBP, temperature, CO2 — each parameter fails in its own way, and most failures are accessories. This course teaches the engineer to test every parameter with a simulator, separate accessory faults from module faults and maintain monitors to a standard that survives an audit.

## SE AI — troubleshooting assistant

- [SE AI](https://serviceengineer.academy/ai/): describe a fault on medical equipment and get a step-by-step check plan grounded in real repair cases and service documentation; it does not invent part numbers. 3 free questions after sign-up; included for 3 months with any course; or $12 a month.
- [SE AI vs ChatGPT](https://serviceengineer.academy/ai/vs-chatgpt/): how a troubleshooting assistant grounded in service manuals and field cases differs from general-purpose AI, and when to use which.
- [Connect SE AI to Claude or ChatGPT (MCP)](https://serviceengineer.academy/ai/connect/): MCP server https://api.serviceengineer.academy/mcp

## For companies

- [Training for teams](https://serviceengineer.academy/teams/): one table of every engineer's courses, exam scores and certificates; training records as PDF or CSV for JCI and ISO audits; assign courses with due dates. 5 seats for the price of 4. Example company: https://api.serviceengineer.academy/training?demo=1
- [How to document the competency of biomedical engineers](https://serviceengineer.academy/guides/document-biomedical-engineer-competency/): what auditors look for and a simple training record that holds up, with what ISO 13485 clause 6.2 and ISO 9001 clause 7.2 expect and a CSV template
- [Factory vs independent service training](https://serviceengineer.academy/guides/factory-vs-independent-service-training/): when engineers need manufacturer training, when vendor-neutral courses are enough, and how to combine both
- [How to run training for a team of service engineers](https://serviceengineer.academy/guides/team-training-service-engineers/): skills matrix, course assignment, assessment, records and refresher dates
